summary: Lolo National Forest lookout in Powell County, Montana: a 30-foot pole tower built 1933, abandoned 1947, burned about 2000 per firelookout.com; now gone.

facts.design: 30-foot pole L-4 tower with a crow's nest about 1/8 mile northwest
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts lists the tower as Removed; firelookout.com says it burned about 2000

events.note: 30-foot pole tower with a crow's nest 1/8 mile northwest, built in 1933 per firelookout.com
Abandoned in 1947 per firelookout.com; a later map label is covered in resolved_conflicts
firelookout.com says the tower burned about 2000; the year is approximate

evidence.supports: 30-foot pole tower with crow's nest 1/8 mile northwest, built 1933, abandoned 1947
evidence.quote: This 30' pole L-4 tower, along with a crow's nest 1/8 mile northwest, built in 1933, were abandoned in 1947.

evidence.supports: about 14 miles east of Seeley Lake, Lolo National Forest (Powell County is supported by cite 2)
Montana Lookouts list: Center Ridge, Powell County, Tower, status Gone
Forest Lookouts lists the Center Ridge tower as Removed
evidence.quote: CENTER RIDGE Lolo National Forest 17N-2W-30 Removed

evidence.supports: a USGS topographic map of Dunham Point documents a Center Ridge Lookout Tower
evidence.quote: including the Center Ridge Lookout Tower and the Monture Creek Guard Station

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says Removed with no cause; firelookout.com says it burned about 2000. Both say it is gone. The story gives the fire from firelookout.com and the removal from Forest Lookouts, and does not combine them into one cause.

firelookout.com dates abandonment to 1947, but a map described by Pastmaps as documenting a Center Ridge Lookout Tower is titled 1968 and marked published 1970. The sources do not say whether a structure stood then, so the story reports both without choosing.

notes_for_editor: Dates (1933, 1947, about 2000) rest on one site, firelookout.com, which also says the tower was a 30-foot pole L-4 tower with a crow's nest. Forest Lookouts and the FFLA list only give Removed and Gone. The Pastmaps map label (1968, published 1970) is the only later reference and does not say whether a structure stood. Brief record was right on status, kind and coordinates; added design and height. Elevation 7,017 ft per firelookout.com has no facts key, so it is left out of the JSON. No staffing, access or photo data found. Web searches used: 2.
